posts.text:
In general, I have never seen Prime Minister Modi give negative signals in public.

I felt the seriousness when he said this in May:

"First came the corona pandemic; then wars began to break out, and now there is an energy crisis. This decade is turning into a decade of disasters for the world.

If these situations are not rapidly changed, the achievements of the past many decades would be washed away, and a huge section of the world’s population would be pushed back into poverty."

It is five months since he said this. Things have only become much worse in that period.

The relationship with the United States is at all time low, and one can even argue that America is now hostile to India.

America wanted a relationship with India to balance China’s power.

China is now in a different league. The revived term for the United States and China is “G2.” So the argument runs that the US no longer sees any "use" for India.

The US has been a major export market and a provider of capital and technology for India.

So I believe the US will only try to create more problems and difficulties for our country.

India has been aware of this shift, though it has only recently begun to give formal, fitting responses to America.

India has developed several sources for its energy and fertiliser needs.

We are also trying to create and expand new markets for our exports.

But with El Nino, high inflation, interest rate hikes, huge shipping costs, supply chains breaking down and pushing up prices for many things, including food, rupee depreciation, and capital outflows, we face many headwinds.

Added to this is AI disruption of white collar jobs.

As I shared recently, everyone from a PMO official to the Chief Economic Adviser to the External Affairs Minister has conveyed the above, in different words and as mildly as possible.

There is not much an individual can do.

As I have been repeating, an emergency fund to cover three years of expenses, not borrowing, spending on needs, and postponing wants until better times are what we can do.

As a country, we need to face this tough period together.

If you read economic history and cycles, you realise these kinds of tough times do not last forever.

In good times, we think they will continue forever.

In bad times, we think we are doomed forever.

Neither is true.

Everything is a cycle.

No one can avoid cycles.

The best we can do, as individuals, companies, or a country, is to be as prepared as our circumstances allow to face those cycles.
